findings.title: Quantity matcher fails open to 1.0 on unknown unit pairs → 10×+ cost-linked QTO error
findings.description: _get_unit_conversion returns UNIT_CONVERSIONS.get(..., 1.0) when the (from,to) pair is absent. The table only covers sf/m2, cy/m3, lf/m, lb/kg (and reverses). Common BIM aliases (sqft, ft, yd3, mm2, in) and mixed casings after normalize still miss → factor stays 1.0. match_element stores that factor; generate_cost_linked_qto multiplies bim_quantity * factor * unit_cost with Confidence still HIGH/MEDIUM from text similarity.
findings.impact: BIM takeoffs in imperial/alias units are priced as if already in CWICR metric units. PoC: 10,000 sqft @ $85/m2 → $850,000 instead of ~$78,968 (10.76× overstatement), poisoning bids, budgets, and procurement orders.
attack_path: Export Revit/IFC QTO with Unit='sqft' (or ft/yd3) while CWICR work items use m2/m3.
CWICRQuantityMatcher.match_quantities / match_element calls _get_unit_conversion('sqft','m2') → 1.0.
generate_cost_linked_qto computes Quantity=bim_qty*1.0 and Total Cost=qty*unit_cost.
Estimator/agent exports Excel or feeds cost calculator → inflated (or wrong-direction) bid.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not location-factor/rate-updater overwrite. Distinct fail-open unit gate on BIM→CWICR matching that prior CWICR/money hunts did not file. Not open-estimate calculator discard — this is systematic conversion silence into cost-linked QTO.

findings.title: Cost calculator falls back to regex str.contains and prices the first match
findings.description: When work_item_code is not an exact index hit, calculate_item_cost uses DataFrame.str.contains(work_item_code, case=False) with pandas default regex=True, then takes matches.iloc[0]. Attacker- or BIM-supplied substrings/metacharacters (GOLD, CONC, .*, A.*) select an unintended row. Status remains CALCULATED (not MISSING_DATA). Same path multiplies labor/material/equipment by unbounded quantity (including negative → credit invert).
findings.impact: Wrong CWICR row drives labor/material/equipment/overhead/profit. PoC: code 'GOLD' (not in index) matches GOLD-999 → ~$6.96M for qty 100; negative qty on CONC-001 yields -$21,505 credit line that reduces estimate totals.
attack_path: Submit estimate line with work_item_code that is not exact (partial trade prefix, typo, or regex like 'GOLD' / '.*').
Exact index lookup fails; str.contains(regex) returns one or more rows; iloc[0] wins.
calculate_item_cost / calculate_estimate marks status=CALCULATED with that row's rates × quantity.
Summary/report uses forged line totals for bid or change pricing.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not rate-updater (no DB mutate) or overhead-markup (rates come from wrong item selection via regex injection/partial match). Not bid-analyzer. New leftover cost-calculator surface.

findings.title: Earned-value progress percent uncapped → forged EV/SPI/CPI/EAC
findings.description: calculate_earned_value trusts progress[activity_id] with no clamp to [0,100]. EV = sum(budgeted_cost * progress/100) can exceed BAC. SPI=EV/PV and CPI=EV/AC then inflate; EAC=BAC/CPI collapses. Callers (agents/field apps) supply the progress dict with no authZ or evidence gate.
findings.impact: Over-reported percent complete forges schedule/cost health: PoC BAC=$1M + progress 250% → EV=$2.5M, SPI=6.25, CPI=5.56, EAC=$180k despite AC=$450k — hides overruns and unlocks optimistic cash/claims decisions.
attack_path: Build activities with real budgeted_cost via create_schedule_activity.
Call calculate_earned_value(..., progress={'A1': 250}, actual_costs={'A1': 450000}, data_date=...).
Observe EV=2.5×BAC, SPI/CPI ≫ 1, EAC ≪ BAC.
Export/report metrics used for owner reporting or payment/claims support.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Distinct from schedule-compression trusting is_critical / false achieved_reduction. This is uncapped percent-complete mass-assignment on CWICR schedule-integrator EVM, not CPM compression.
key_snippets: ev = sum(a.budgeted_cost * progress.get(a.activity_id, 0) / 100 for a in activities)
spi = ev / pv if pv > 0 else 0
cpi = ev / ac if ac > 0 else 0

findings.title: get_work_item_cost returns 0 for unknown codes → silent cost-loaded underbid
findings.description: get_work_item_cost returns 0 when the code is missing from the CWICR index (no error, no MISSING_DATA flag). create_schedule_activity still appends the code to work_items and sets budgeted_cost from the zeroed sum. generate_cash_flow / calculate_earned_value then treat the activity as low/zero budget.
findings.impact: Typos, attacker-chosen fake codes, or stripped rates silently drop entire scopes from cost-loaded schedules and cash-flow projections → understated bids and BAC.
attack_path: Include work_items with codes absent from CWICR (or empty dataset index).
create_schedule_activity sums get_work_item_cost → 0 while still listing the codes.
generate_cash_flow / EVM use budgeted_cost=0 for those activities.
Project cash/BAC understates true scope; bid or funding decision proceeds.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not cost-calculator MISSING_DATA path (that skill flags status). Not rate-updater. Fail-open zero-price on schedule cost integration specifically.
key_snippets:
if self._code_index is None or code not in self._code_index.index:
            return 0

findings.title: Labor scheduler caps workers_needed but keeps full total_hours (silent understaff)
findings.description: generate_schedule computes workers=ceil(hours/hours_per_day) then workers=min(workers, max_workers_per_trade) (default 50) without reducing total_hours, raising an error, or setting a shortage flag. peak_workers and daily_loading reflect the capped headcount while assignment.total_hours and schedule.total_labor_hours still encode the uncapped demand.
findings.impact: Plans look staffed at ≤50/trade while hundreds of hours/day remain unallocated → crew shortfall, overtime surprise, and safety understaffing on high-quantity packages.
attack_path: Submit high-quantity / short-duration items so daily trade hours require >50 workers (or lower max_workers_per_trade).
generate_schedule caps workers_needed at max_workers_per_trade.
CrewAssignment still stores total_hours=uncapped hours; peak_workers uses capped day_total.
Export/loading curve used for hiring shows peak=50 while work implies 100 → understaffed execution.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Opposite of already-reported resource-pool max-vs-sum overbook. This is fail-open capacity understaff with no shortage signal — not double-booking.

findings.title: Equipment planner merges concurrent same-type demand into one unit by stretching days
findings.description: extract_equipment_requirements aggregates by equipment description: hours are summed and start/end span the union of activities. Only one EquipmentItem is emitted; days_needed=ceil(hours/8) stretches the rental instead of adding units when concurrent daily demand exceeds one machine's 8h capacity. generate_equipment_plan schedule lists a single description per day.
findings.impact: Two overlapping excavation packages that each need a full-time excavator are planned as one longer rental → on-site capacity shortfall / false availability.
attack_path: Submit two items sharing equipment description with overlapping start_day/duration and high equipment_norm*qty.
Aggregator merges hours and min/max days into one equip_key.
One EquipmentItem created; schedule appends one description per date.
Field follows plan expecting one machine for concurrent scopes.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not fleet-manager double-book IN_USE or site-logistics crane tonnage. CWICR equipment-planner specific merge-by-description capacity ignore.

poc.behavior: concurrent full-time demand merged to single unit with stretched days

findings.title: Report generator interpolates unsanitized project/category/line fields into HTML
findings.description: add_breakdown_by_category, add_line_items, and generate_html embed category, description, code, and project_name into HTML via f-strings with no escaping. save_html writes the raw string to output_path.
findings.impact: Stored XSS when the HTML report is opened in a browser (session/cookie theft, fake bid figures in DOM).
attack_path: Supply project_name or category/description containing <script> or event-handler markup.
Generator builds sections/html with raw interpolation.
save_html writes cost_report.html.
Victim opens report → script executes in report origin.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior clash to_html XSS near-miss was discarded because pandas escaped. This skill writes raw f-string HTML with no escape.

findings.title: create_assembly silently overwrites existing assembly_code templates
findings.description: create_assembly always does self._assemblies[assembly_code]=assembly with no existence check, authZ, or version conflict. quantity_per_unit is unbounded (including 0/negative). apply_assembly then prices from the replaced template.
findings.impact: Canonical assemblies (e.g. SLAB-100 from create_standard_assemblies) can be replaced with near-zero-cost item sets → understated estimates wherever the code is reused.
attack_path: create_standard_assemblies() or load library with SLAB-100 at real cost.
Call create_assembly(assembly_code='SLAB-100', items=[{'code':'X','quantity_per_unit':0}, ...]).
Dict entry overwritten; apply_assembly('SLAB-100', qty) returns near-zero total_cost.
Downstream estimate/export uses poisoned template.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not cwicr-location-factor add_location rate overwrite and not rate-updater. This is assembly-template library overwrite on leftover assembly-builder.

apply_assembly location_factor unbounded — location-factor known class.
waste-calculator custom_factors negative/unbounded — soft factor class; weaker than quantity-matcher fail-open into QTO money.
historical-cost complete_project status forge + suggest_adjustment_factors poison — analytics/benchmark only; weaker than permit ISSUED / EVM forge SoR.
crew-optimizer / takeoff / unit-converter negative or default bar_size=1.0 — calculator-only; unit helper fail-open weak.
productivity-tracker planned_quantity=actual_quantity — analytics tautology, no payment SoR.
data-loader / export output_path traversal — same class as already-reported csv-handler / bim-cost path writes.
data-loader / multilingual str.contains regex ReDoS — DoS without money/safety SoR.

comparison-tool — pure variance math; no forge/authZ sink.
semantic-search-cwicr — Qdrant/OpenAI wiring; no business-logic forge in skill body.
